questions.title: A ten-place linear queue
questions.statement:
1 A program stores integer data in a linear queue.

 The queue is created as a global 1D array with space for 10 elements.

 The queue has a global head pointer, initialised to –1, that points to the first element in
 the queue.

 The queue has a global tail pointer, initialised to –1, that points to the last element in the queue.

## 1(a) The main program initialises the 10 elements of the queue to –1 and initialises the
 two pointers.

 Write program code to declare the global variables and initialise the queue and its pointers.

 Save your program as Question1_J26.

 Copy and paste the program code into 1(a) in the evidence document.

 [3]

## 1(b) The function Enqueue() performs these tasks:

- takes an integer parameter
- checks if the queue is full
- returns Boolean FALSE, if the queue is full
- stores the parameter in the queue, updates the appropriate pointer(s) and returns
 Boolean TRUE, if the queue is not full.

 Write program code for Enqueue()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 1(b) in the evidence document.
 [7]

## 1(c) (i) Write program code to extend the main program to:

- take 11 integers as input from the user
- use the appropriate function to insert each integer into the queue
- output a message if at any point the queue is full
- output the final content of the queue array. Do not dequeue the data.

 You do not need to validate the data input.

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 1(c)(i) in the evidence document.

 [5]

### (ii) Test your program.

 Enter the following data as input in the order given:

 Take a screenshot of the output(s).

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the screenshot into 1(c)(ii) in the evidence document.
 [1]

## 1(d) The function Dequeue():

- returns –1 if the queue is empty
- updates the pointer(s) and returns the next item from the queue if the queue is
 not empty.

 Write program code for Dequeue()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 1(d) in the evidence document.

 [6]

## 1(e) (i) Write program code to amend the main program to:

- take 6 integers as input from the user and store them in the queue using the
 appropriate function
- use the appropriate function to remove 4 elements from the queue
- output each removed element from the queue.

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 1(e)(i) in the evidence document.
 [3]

### (ii) Test your program.

 Enter the following data as input in the order given:

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the screenshot into 1(e)(ii) in the evidence document.

questions.title: Toy records and selection files
questions.statement:
> **Classroom replacement data:** The original candidate file `Toys.txt` was not supplied. This practice includes a synthetic 16-record replacement with the required format; only the first example record comes from the question paper. File-dependent classroom output differs from the original examination data.

2 A program stores data about toys that are made from bricks. The toys are stored in a record
 structure with four fields:

- ToyName: the string name of the toy
- NumberBricks: the integer number of bricks in the toy
- Difficulty: the string difficulty level of the toy (easy, medium or expert)
- Category: the string category of the toy (for example town, display, play).

## 2(a) Write program code to declare a record structure with the identifier ToyRecord and the
 four fields.

 Save your program as Question2_J26.

 Copy and paste the program code into 2(a) in the evidence document.

 [2]

## 2(b) The text file Toys.txt stores data about 16 toys. Each toy is on a new line in the file. The
 data is stored in the order: toy name, number of bricks, difficulty, category. Each value is
 separated by a comma.

 For example, the first line in the file is:

 Fire Station,3981,Expert,Town

 The name of the toy is Fire Station. The toy has 3981 bricks. The difficulty level is Expert.
 The category is Town.

## 2(i) The function ReadData():

- takes an array of type ToyRecord as a parameter
- opens the file Toys.txt and reads in the data
- creates a new record of type ToyRecord for each toy read from the file
- stores each record in the parameter array
- returns the populated array.

 The function uses exception handling when opening and reading from the file.

 Write program code for ReadData()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 2(b)(i) in the evidence document.
 [8]

### (ii) The procedure OutputToys() takes an array of type ToyRecord as a parameter and
 outputs the data for each toy in the array.

 Write program code for OutputToys()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 2(b)(ii) in the evidence document.

 [3]

### (iii) Write program code for the main program to:

- declare an array of type ToyRecord with space for 16 elements
- call the function ReadData() with the empty array and store the returned array
- call OutputToys() with the returned array.

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 2(b)(iii) in the evidence document.
 [3]

### (iv) Test your program.

 Take a screenshot of the output(s).

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the screenshot into 2(b)(iv) in the evidence document.
 [1]

## 2(c) The program needs to allow a user to enter the difficulty level of a toy and then write all toys
 that match that difficulty level to an external text file.

## 2(i) The function SearchToys():

- takes an array of type ToyRecord as a parameter
- prompts the user to enter the difficulty level
- takes the difficulty level as input until it is valid
- creates a new array containing the ToyRecord objects that match the difficulty
 level input
- returns the populated array.

 Write program code for SearchToys()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 2(c)(i) in the evidence document.
 [5]

### (ii) The procedure WriteToys():

- takes an array of type ToyRecord as a parameter
- creates and opens the file SelectedToys.txt to write
- writes each record from ToyRecord to SelectedToys.txt with each field
 separated by a comma and each record on a new line. For example:

 <ToyName>,<NumberBricks>,<Difficulty>,<Category>

 Write program code for WriteToys()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 2(c)(ii) in the evidence document.

 [3]

### (iii) Write program code to extend the main program to:

- call SearchToys() with the populated array and store the return array
- call WriteToys() with the returned array.

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 2(c)(iii) in the evidence document.
 [2]

### (iv) Test your program. Enter the appropriate input for a medium difficulty level
 when prompted.

 Take one screenshot of the text file the program produces with the contents and
 filename clearly visible.

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the screenshot into 2(c)(iv) in the evidence document.
 [1]

questions.title: Objects along a path
questions.statement:
3 A prototype for a game is designed using Object‑Oriented Programming (OOP).

 The game will allow a character to move along a path (for example a road or sidewalk).

 The prototype requires the classes setting up and the path creating ready for the character to
 be implemented.

## 3(a) Each space in the path can contain an object. The path and objects are created as classes.

 The class TheObject stores the data about the objects. The attributes are public.

 TheObject
 ObjectType : String stores the type of object, either "Money" or "Experience"

 Amount : Integer stores the amount of the object, for example 200
 Constructor() initialises the attributes to the parameter values

 The class Path stores the data about the objects. The attributes are public.

 Path
 BoardArray[0:99] : TheObject an array of 100 objects of type TheObject

 NumberSpaces : Integer stores the number of spaces in the path
 Constructor() initialises NumberSpaces to the parameter value.
 Initialises all 100 array objects to an empty object of type
 TheObject. An empty object has the values
 ObjectType = "" and Amount = –1

 GetNumberSpaces() returns NumberSpaces

 InitialiseData() takes an array of objects of type TheObject as a
 parameter and stores them in BoardArray

 ReturnPath() returns a string created using data from each object
 in BoardArray

 GetPathObject() takes a number as a parameter and returns the object in
 that index in BoardArray

## 3(i) Write program code to declare the class TheObject and its constructor.

 Use your programming language appropriate constructor.

 If you are writing in Python, include attribute declarations using comments.

 Save your program as Question3_J26.

 Copy and paste the program code into 3(a)(i) in the evidence document.
 [4]

### (ii) Write program code to declare the class Path, its constructor and
 method GetNumberSpaces()

 Use your programming language appropriate constructor.

 Do not declare the other methods.

 If you are writing in Python, include attribute declarations using comments.

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 3(a)(ii) in the evidence document.

 [4]

### (iii) The method InitialiseData() takes an array of type TheObject as a parameter.

 The method stores each element from the parameter array into the array BoardArray
 in the same order.

 If there are more objects in the parameter array than in NumberSpaces, the method
 does not store the data and returns FALSE. Otherwise, it returns TRUE

 Write program code for InitialiseData()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 3(a)(iii) in the evidence document.
 [3]

### (iv) The method ReturnPath() creates and returns a string containing the type and
 amount of each object that is not a null object in BoardArray, in the format:

 <ObjectType>-<Amount>

 For example, an array with two not null objects produces the string:

 Money-100 Experience-50

 You can assume that there will always be an object that is not null in BoardArray

 Write program code for ReturnPath()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 3(a)(iv) in the evidence document.
 [2]

## 3(v) The method GetPathObject() takes an integer index as a parameter and returns the
 object at the parameter index in BoardArray

 Write program code for GetPathObject()

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 3(a)(v) in the evidence document.

 [1]

## 3(b) (i) Write program code for the main program to:

- create a new array, ArrayOfObjects, of type TheObject with five spaces
- store the following objects in each space in ArrayOfObjects in the order given:
 money with amount 50
 experience with amount 100
 money with amount 200
 money with amount 20
 experience with amount 30
- create a new object, Path1, of type Path with five spaces
- call InitialiseData() for Path1 with ArrayOfObjects
- call ReturnPath() for Path1 and output the return value.

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the program code into 3(b)(i) in the evidence document.
 [6]

### (ii) Test your program.

 Take a screenshot of the output(s).

 Save your program.

 Copy and paste the screenshot into 3(b)(ii) in the evidence document.
 [1]

referenceSolutions.Q1:
Queue = [-1] * 10
HeadPointer = -1
TailPointer = -1

def Enqueue(Data):
    global HeadPointer, TailPointer
    if TailPointer == 9: return False
    TailPointer += 1
    Queue[TailPointer] = Data
    if HeadPointer == -1: HeadPointer = 0
    return True

def Dequeue():
    global HeadPointer
    if HeadPointer == -1 or HeadPointer > TailPointer: return -1
    Data = Queue[HeadPointer]
    HeadPointer += 1
    return Data

# Final main program, amended by part (e). Part (c)'s earlier 11-input run is evidence.
for i in range(6):
    Value = int(input("Enter integer: "))
    if not Enqueue(Value): print("Queue is full")
for i in range(4): print(Dequeue())
